headline: Software Surges as Semis Sink: Tuesday's Session Splits Along a Sharp Divide
body_html:
Midway through Tuesday's session, the broader market is holding a constructive tone, with advancers outpacing decliners by a roughly 321-to-178 margin across the 501-name universe. Software leads all sectors with a gain of 3.23%, followed by Consumer at 2.48% and Homebuilders at 1.58%, painting a picture of rotation into rate-sensitive and growth-oriented names as investors parse expectations ahead of Federal Reserve commentary later this week.

The session's headline mover is Robert Half, the staffing and professional-services firm, which is up 12.61% and ranks as the day's top gainer — a notable lift for a name tied to labor-market sentiment. Autodesk follows closely at 10.06%, adding credibility to the Software sector's leadership, while Abercrombie & Fitch and e.l.f. Beauty, up 9.31% and 8.60% respectively, underscore the Consumer sector's broad participation.

The sharp counterpoint lies in semiconductors and their supply-chain ecosystem. Energy is the weakest sector at -2.05%, with Semiconductors close behind at -1.48%. Veeco Instruments (-11.16%), Sandisk (-11.02%), and Ichor Holdings (-9.53%) are pacing the decline. Heading into the close, watch whether the semi-equipment selloff deepens or stabilizes — and whether Consumer momentum holds.

briefs.headline: Robert Half Surges 12% on Staffing Sentiment Shift
briefs.body: Robert Half is the session's standout mover, surging 12.61% midday. The professional-staffing firm's sharp advance suggests investors are reassessing labor-market durability, a meaningful signal given the broader debate over whether white-collar hiring trends are stabilizing or still under pressure heading into second-half 2026.

briefs.headline: Semi-Equipment Names Absorb Heavy Selling Pressure
briefs.body: Veeco Instruments, Ichor Holdings, and Axcelis Technologies are each down between 9% and 11% Tuesday, dragging the broader semiconductor-equipment group sharply lower. The cluster of declines points to supply-chain caution rather than any single earnings catalyst, and raises questions about near-term capital spending commitments among chipmakers.

briefs.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Language in Focus as Rate Uncertainty Lingers
briefs.body: Prediction-market traders are closely scrutinizing the phrasing Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh may deploy this week, with particular attention to words associated with inflationary shock. Bitcoin ETFs snapped a recent inflow streak amid growing rate-cut skepticism, suggesting risk appetite is selectively cooling ahead of any policy signal.

briefs.headline: Gold Edges Higher as Geopolitical Tension Temporarily Eases
briefs.body: Gold futures are climbing Tuesday as a pause in West Asia hostilities temporarily reduces immediate inflation-risk fears, allowing safe-haven demand to build on macro uncertainty rather than crisis pricing. The move reflects a nuanced bid — investors seeking insurance against policy missteps rather than outright geopolitical catastrophe.

briefs.headline: Crude Futures Signal Pragmatism Over Peace Optimism
briefs.body: Oil markets are trading in a manner that reflects structural adaptability rather than any meaningful hope for a near-term resolution to Middle East tensions, according to analyst commentary. Energy is the weakest sector midday at -2.05%, consistent with the market's view that supply dynamics, not diplomacy, are the dominant crude price driver.

briefs.headline: Consumer Names Provide Broad Ballast as Apparel and Cosmetics Pop
briefs.body: Beyond Robert Half's standout move, the Consumer sector is benefiting from broad participation Tuesday. Abercrombie & Fitch is up 9.31% and e.l.f. Beauty has added 8.60%, suggesting that spending-resilience narratives are finding buyers at current levels even as macro crosscurrents persist into the back half of the year.
